topic.title: Workspace Translation Jobs View
topic.shortdesc: Use the Translation Jobs view to start translation jobs, track their progress, and bring the results into your workspace.

body.p: The Translation Jobs view (found inside the project's Personal Workspace) lists the workspace translation jobs, each displayed as a card. This is where you start a new job and track or manage jobs that are already running or finished. For details about what a translation job does, see Translation.

p.note: The view is only available when the AI features are enabled for your organization.

body.p: While a job is pending or running, the number of those jobs is shown as a badge next to the Translation Jobs icon in the left vertical stripe, so you can leave the view and still see that work is in progress.

section.title: Starting a New Job
section.p: Use the New button at the top of the view to open the New translation dialog box, where you can choose one or more publications, one or more target languages, and optional instructions for the agent. A single job covers everything that you selected and processes the target languages one after another. You can also open the same dialog box using the New translation action in the Publication view. See The First Time You Translate a Project.
The list updates automatically while jobs are in progress. Use the Refresh button at the top of the view to reload it on demand.

section.title: How the Jobs Are Listed
section.p: Jobs are listed with the most recent first and grouped by the day they were created (Today, Yesterday, then the date for earlier days). Each card shows:

ul.li: The target language of the job, in the form French translation. If the job covers several languages, the remaining ones are counted (for example, French + 2 more) and listed in the tooltip.
The publications covered by the job, counted and listed in a tooltip in the same way.
When the job finished (or when it was created if it has not finished yet). The tooltip shows the exact date and how long the job took.
The current state of the job, described below.

section.p: If no job has been started yet, the view shows a No jobs yet. message.

section.title: Job States
section.p: A job goes through the following states:

dlentry.dd: The job was accepted but has not started yet because the server is busy with other jobs. The card shows a progress indicator.
The agent is processing the job. The card shows a progress indicator and the step that the agent is currently performing (for example, Translating files…).
The job finished successfully, and its results can be brought into your workspace.
The job stopped because of an error. The card shows a Translation failed message, and the reason is recorded in the execution log. A failed job may still have produced some translated files.
The job was stopped before it finished, and the card shows a Translation was stopped message.

section.title: Actions Available on a Job Card
section.p: Depending on the state of the job, the following actions are available on its card, either directly or from the Job actions vertical ellipsis (3 vertical dots) drop-down menu:

dlentry.dd: Opens the Execution log dialog box, which updates live while the job is running. Once the job has finished, you can save the log as a text file using Download log. See Checking the Job Log.
Stops the job. This action is available while the job is pending or running. You are asked to confirm the action.

Adds the files produced by the job to your workspace so you can review and commit them. If the workspace contains locally modified files that the import would overwrite, an Import conflict dialog box lets you either overwrite those files or close the dialog box and commit your changes first.
This action is available for a failed job that produced some files. It imports the work completed before the failure so that it is not lost.
Starts a new job with the same publications, target languages, and instructions.
Removes the Integrated badge and makes Bring into workspace available again, for example, after you discarded the imported changes. See Tracking Which Jobs You Have Brought into Your Workspace.
This action is available for a finished job. It removes the job and its results. You are asked to confirm the action, which cannot be undone.
